why: Return to RQ-1 after EP-0016..EP-0028 drifted into detector, publication and reader audits. RQ-1 names four frictions; gang/locality (H10, C-009) is the only one never measured. E18 asks whether node fragmentation reverses the ranking of size-first policies against FCFS + EASY backfill, and whether locality-aware placement removes that effect.

prior_art.why_this_block_exists: Required since PRED-016: this domain rediscovered two known results before checking the literature.
already_known: Locality and consolidation matter for distributed training throughput; Tiresias (Gu et al., NSDI 2019) finds placement sensitivity depends on the model and relaxes consolidation for insensitive jobs.
Analysis of Microsoft's Philly cluster (Jeon et al., USENIX ATC 2019) reports that gang scheduling with locality constraints increases queueing delay and lowers utilization.
Gandiva (Xiao et al., OSDI 2018) uses packing and migration to reduce fragmentation.
Topology-aware GPU placement (e.g., Amaral et al., SC 2017) improves job performance on multi-GPU nodes.
prior_art.what_is_not_claimed_new: That fragmentation hurts, and that consolidated placement helps, are known.
prior_art.candidate_contribution: Within the MSJ model: whether fragmentation acts as a ranking friction between size-first ordering (greedy SRPT, ServerFilling-SRPT) and FCFS/EASY backfill, and whether a simple best-fit compact placement neutralises it. Not checked against the literature systematically; novelty UNKNOWN.
prior_art.search_done: Recall only; no systematic search before sealing.

seen: c12 capacities at pi=0 (used to choose loads 0.6/0.7 below every capacity lower bound).
E1 rankings at rho=0.85 without locality.
Runtime of one 20k-job pilot per mix x policy at pi=0.3 first_fit; timings were printed, metrics were not.

The penalty_mode='excess' change was made because under the existing 'all' mode a 64-GPU gang pays for 7 unavoidable nodes, which would drive every gang_heavy cell over capacity regardless of placement. This was reasoned from the formula, not from runs.
seal_integrity.not_seen: No E18 metric at any pi > 0 before sealing.
seal_integrity.timestamp: Local git commit only; no external timestamp.

measurand_validity.model: 8-GPU nodes; rate = 1 / (1 + pi * excess_nodes), excess = nodes spanned beyond ceil(need/8). Sticky placement, no migration. Placement never blocks admission. Real cross-node slowdown depends on model and interconnect; pi is a knob, not a measured value.
measurand_validity.loads: rho 0.6 and 0.7 are nominal loads under ideal placement; fragmentation raises effective load and may push a cell over. That is an outcome, labelled three-way.
measurand_validity.not_modelled: Locality-aware admission (delaying a job to wait for a compact slot), migration, network topology beyond nodes.

experiment.analysis: analyze_e18.py (written and sealed with this file)
experiment.grid: 2 mixes (trace_like, gang_heavy) x 4 policies (fcfs, easy_backfill, srpt, sf_srpt) x rho {0.6, 0.7} x pi {0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.6} x placement {first_fit, compact} x seeds {1801, 1802, 1803} x horizons {40k, 80k} = 768 runs
experiment.fixed: N=64, node 8, sigma 0, c_pre 0, exponential sizes mean 1, backlog cap 6000, t_limit_factor 2.0

detector.label: DIVERGING if aborted/time limit or alpha >= 0.8; STABLE if alpha <= 0.2; else UNKNOWN. Cell label requires all three seeds to agree.
detector.status: alpha is unaudited near a boundary (U-31: threshold 0.5 misclassifies within about 1% of capacity). The 0.2/0.8 band leaves the ambiguous middle as UNKNOWN instead of forcing a verdict. UNKNOWN cells are excluded from comparisons and counted.

predictions.P0: Control (instrument check, forced by the model): at pi = 0, first_fit and compact give exactly equal mean JCT in every run. Failure stops the episode as R3.
predictions.P1: At pi = 0.3, compact spans fewer excess nodes per placement than first_fit in every mix x policy x rho, and at most 0.05 on gang_heavy.
predictions.P2: first_fit, rho 0.7, pi 0 -> 0.3: mean-JCT degradation factor is larger on gang_heavy than trace_like for every policy that is STABLE in all four cells.
predictions.P3: DECISION. Pair reversal between pi 0 and 0.6 (strict: ratio < 0.95 vs > 1.05 with both STABLE, or STABLE vs DIVERGING): at least one reversal under first_fit across mix x rho, and none under compact.
predictions.P4: trace_like, first_fit, pi 0 -> 0.6: easy_backfill has the smallest degradation factor among policies STABLE at both ends, at both rho.
predictions.P5: gang_heavy, first_fit, rho 0.7, pi 0.6: sf_srpt degrades by a larger factor than easy_backfill (sf_srpt DIVERGING with easy_backfill STABLE counts as larger).

pre_committed_consequence.P3_pass: Report locality as a ranking friction under naive placement that compact placement neutralises, within this model.
pre_committed_consequence.P3_fail_no_first_fit_reversal: Report that fragmentation does not reorder these policies at these loads; locality is then a level effect, not a ranking friction. Do not search other loads or penalties for a reversal in this episode.
pre_committed_consequence.P3_fail_compact_reversal: Report that best-fit compact placement does not remove the ranking effect.

declared_unknowns: Loads above 0.7, where capacity differences start to dominate.
rules: No edits to this file, run_e18.py or analyze_e18.py after the sealing commit.
If more than one third of cells are UNKNOWN, report that before any grade interpretation.
Keep failed predictions; do not re-grade with new thresholds.
